abstract: Exploration quality and policy parameter updates influence the training of deterministic actor–critic controllers. This study presents ES–TD3, an evolution strategy-assisted Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient framework that combines population-based actor-parameter search with off-policy learning. Candidate actors undergo Gaussian perturbation, episodic evaluation, elite selection, and fitness-weighted recombination. The mathematical analysis establishes that the recombined parameter vector lies within the convex hull of the elite actors and bounds its displacement from the current population center by the largest elite displacement, with a perturbation-dependent bound for Gaussian candidates. For a mass–spring–damper plant with positive mass, damping, and stiffness, bounded-input/bounded-state and Lyapunov analyses establish uniform ultimate boundedness of the physical state under the bounded deterministic actor output. These guarantees concern individual recombination steps and plant-state boundedness, not asymptotic tracking or global training convergence. MATLAB/Simulink simulations compare ES–TD3 with standard TD3 and PID control, examine reference and initial condition variations, and assess sensitivity to evolutionary settings. The best observed configuration reaches the moving-average reward threshold of 126,500 at generation 203 and attains a final moving-average reward of 126,512. The reported ES–TD3 run exhibits smoother reward progression than the TD3 baseline, while the deployed policy produces bounded tracking responses across the tested scenarios. The results support the feasibility of combining evolutionary policy search with actor–critic learning for the considered control problem; broader performance claims require independent repeated trials.
title: Evolution Strategy-Assisted TD3 for Continuous Control: Policy-Update Analysis and Plant-State Boundedness

abstract: Distributed zeroth-order optimization has gained increasing attention in applications where exact gradients are computationally expensive or unavailable. However, the iterative exchange of local decision variables makes distributed networks vulnerable to inference attacks. While differential privacy provides a rigorous framework for privacy protection, conventional approaches generally require additional random noise, which inevitably affects optimization accuracy. In this paper, we investigate whether the randomness inherent in zeroth-order estimation can itself provide privacy protection. We develop a distributed zeroth-order gradient descent method that integrates consensus updates with a ball-uniform two-point gradient estimator. Our theoretical analysis shows that our algorithm attains standard convergence guarantees in both online and offline optimization settings. We then characterize the relevant probability distributions of the associated privacy mechanism, and establish differential privacy guarantees for both the online and offline optimization settings. These results reveal the potential of intrinsic zeroth-order randomness for privacy protection.
title: Differentially Private Distributed Optimization via the Intrinsic Randomness of Zeroth-Order Estimators: Sampling Geometry, Convergence, and Privacy Guarantees

abstract: We study decentralized composite finite-sum optimization over a fixed connected undirected network, where agents access local component functions through function evaluations and share a possibly nonsmooth convex regularizer. In this setting, standard two-point gradient estimators can retain nonvanishing variance at a solution, complicating their integration with gradient tracking. We propose Distributed Zeroth-Order Incremental Variance Reduction (Distributed ZIVR), which combines incrementally updated component-gradient estimates with a proximal gradient-tracking scheme. The method admits an implementation using a constant number of function evaluations per agent at every iteration, without intermittent full-component or full-coordinate refreshes. For convex smooth component functions and strongly convex local averages, we establish linear convergence up to a controllable finite-difference error. With the finite-difference radius chosen for the target accuracy, Chebyshev-accelerated mixing yields a per-agent oracle complexity of $\widetilde{O}(d(m+κ)\log(1/ε))$ for expected squared solution error $ε$, where $d$ is the dimension, $m$ is the number of components per agent, and $κ$ is the condition number. This matches the centralized ZIVR oracle bound, while the communication bound has only an inverse square-root dependence on the network spectral gap. Experiments on logistic and robust regression demonstrate rapid reduction of solution and consensus errors.
title: Distributed Zeroth-Order Composite Finite-Sum Optimization via Incremental Variance Reduction
